characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm.
Room temperature, initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1.
Cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction by standard metallographic techniques.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five different alloys synthesized in one operation using five Cu molds successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; remaining melt composition adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10 × 50 × 130 mm³ blocks hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Reheated to 1100 °C, water quenched, and cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ segments.
Homogenization at 1100 °C for 2 h under Ar, followed by water quenching.
Aging conducted in air at 550 °C for 24 h, followed by oil quenching (one of the 45 RAP sample conditions).
Scales removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized microstructure with a grain size of ~20 µm and some retained microsegregations of Mn (state after hot rolling and water quenching; as-cast material was coarse dendritic)

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al alloy (and 4Al), the applied aging treatments only very weakly affected the mechanical data, in contrast to the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening) [b0024].

The intermediate Al variants (2–6 wt.% Al) show a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior than the ~8 wt.% Al variant, whose pronounced strengthening is attributed to nm-sized κ-carbides [b0025].

In Figure 4, the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al data points (pooled across aging conditions, not resolved specifically for the 550 °C/24 h condition) lie at approximately 670–770 MPa tensile strength and 30–55% elongation to fracture [figure_004].
The 6 wt.% Al variant is intermediate in mechanical response: its mechanical data fall between those of the Al-free alloy and the 8 wt.% Al alloy [b0024].
